title: Two-degree coherent structure model for a proper flat curve family
statement:
Let $f:X\to S$ be a proper flat morphism of finite presentation of schemes [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-proper-morphism, def-weil-flat-morphism, def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions]. For every $s\in S$ write $X_s=X\times_S\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(s)$ [def-pc-base-change, def-weil-residue-field]. Assume $\dim(X_s)\leq1$ [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension] and that the structural map $\kappa(s)\to H^0(X_s,\mathcal O_{X_s})$ is bijective [pqf-def-cohomology]. Put $K=Rf_*(\mathcal O_X[0])$ [def-pc-derived-category, def-pc-derived-direct-image], and let $u:\mathcal O_S[0]\to K$ be the derived structural unit, whose map on degree-zero cohomology is the structural function pullback. Then $K$ is perfect [def-pc-perfect-complex], $H^0(u):\mathcal O_S\to H^0(K)$ is invertible, and $E=H^1(K)$ is quasi-coherent and finite locally free [pqf-def-coherent, def-sc-finite-locally-free-sheaf]. Zariski-locally on $S$ there is an isomorphism
$$K\cong\mathcal O_S[0]\oplus E[-1],$$
where $E[-1]$ places $E$ in cohomological degree one. In particular $H^i(K)=0$ for $i\notin\{0,1\}$. For every morphism $g:T\to S$, put $X_T=X\times_ST$ and let $f_T:X_T\to T$ be the projection. The canonical derived module base-change map [def-pc-derived-module-base-change-map]
$$\delta_g:Lg^*K\longrightarrow Rf_{T,*}(\mathcal O_{X_T}[0])$$
is an isomorphism; no flatness of $g$, reducedness of $S$, or constancy of the local rank of $E$ on all of $S$ is assumed.

source.place: Tag 0GKA, label lemma-genus-in-nodal-family-of-curves, proof from the local decomposition through the finite-free residue model; the argument uses only proper flat finite presentation, fibrewise constant functions and fibre dimension at most one, rather than the nodal hypothesis.

proof.text: Prove the proper relatively flat single-module perfectness needed here as a private helper, using the supplied global scheme localizations. Descend the morphism and module near a point to a Noetherian stage. At that stage bounded coherent proper direct image is pseudo-coherent; the bounded flat Cech model supplies locally finite Tor dimension. The pseudo-coherent finite-Tor criterion gives perfectness. Canonical relatively flat derived base change identifies the pullback of this perfect object with the original direct image on the neighbourhood. Derived pullback preserves perfectness. Identify the neighbourhood with its open image using recorded composition of pullbacks, and transport its strictly perfect models to the base. Apply this helper to the finitely presented unit module, relatively flat since f is flat.

source.place: Tags 0A1H, 0B91(2), 08E2 and 08CQ; direct derived-object proof, avoiding the archived open-pseudocoherence comparison chain.

proof.text: Perfectness gives quasi-coherent cohomology. The explicit canonical structural-unit properties give negative residue vanishing and invertibility of its residue H0 map. The degree-zero fibre criterion gives invertibility of H0 of this actual unit. Canonical flat invertible-module base change, followed by the canonical single-pullback and unit-pullback comparisons, gives invertibility of exactly the displayed base-change morphism.

source.place: Tag 0E62 and Tag 0GKA, degree-zero unit and canonical structure base change.

proof.text: Each fibre is finite type over its residue field and hence Noetherian. Grothendieck vanishing and dimension at most one kill its structure cohomology above degree one. The higher-direct-image/global-cohomology comparison on the one-point residue spectrum, and the homology comparison for the unbounded right derived functor of a single module, give vanishing of the derived structure image above degree one. Canonical base change transports this to residue pullbacks of K. Together with negative residue vanishing, every residue Betti number outside zero and one is zero. The residue H0 unit gives Betti number one at degree zero.

Apply the finite-free residue model directly to K. Its ranks force terms outside zero and one to vanish and its degree-zero term to have rank one. Represent the canonical structural unit by a chain map on the affine model. The residue-H0 stalk criterion at every point of this open shows its degree-zero component is an isomorphism. Its chain-map equation therefore forces the differential from zero to one to vanish; all other differentials vanish by the support bounds.

source.place: Tag 0GKA and Tag 0BCD: rank-one degree-zero model and the canonical unit.

proof.text: The elementary inclusions and projections split the zero-differential two-term complex as the biproduct of its degree-zero and degree-one singles. Homology of a zero-differential complex is its term, so the restricted H1 is the finite free degree-one term. The neighbourhoods cover the base, giving finite local freeness. The degree-zero term is the unit and the single-functor shift comparison identifies the degree-one single with H1[-1], giving the required local isomorphism. All other homology sheaves vanish locally and hence globally. These steps are proved private categorical glue, with no additional public statements or postponed proofs.

source.place: Tag 0GKA, final local splitting and finite local freeness.

proof_origin.place: Tag 0GKA, applying 0BCD directly to K and using the canonical unit to kill its only differential. Perfectness is proved from geometric Noetherian descent, proper coherence, local finite Tor dimension and canonical relatively flat base change (0A1H/0B91), using the supplied global scheme localizations.

This is a zero-new-node split. The statement is byte-identical to the version Q05 created, and the item is still unsplit in live and side, so no other group has done it. Source: Stacks 0GKA, statement and proof, read in full. The 4 steps follow its proof exactly, with the nodal and connected hypotheses replaced by the facts actually used (proper flat finite presentation, kappa(s) = H^0 of the fibre, fibre dimension at most 1); nothing is weakened. Step 1: 0B91 (lem-pc-rf-perfect-base-change) applies to G = O_X, which is finitely presented and S-flat; it gives perfectness and the canonical def-pc-derived-module-base-change-map isomorphism for arbitrary g, and G_T = O_{X_T}. Step 2: the 0E62 unit lemma (f is quasi-compact separated flat) and the degree-zero criterion give H^0(a) iso and K = O_S + P locally, P of tor amplitude [1,inf). H^0(u) is invertible because H^0(a)e_1 = e_0 f# with e_i isomorphisms; the step's wording is slightly loose but the inference is valid. Step 3: the fibre is finite type over a Noetherian field spectrum, hence Noetherian; 02UZ with topological dimension at most 1 kills H^q for q > 1, and base change along i_s identifies these groups with H^i of the pulled-back complex. Step 4: only d_1 can be nonzero; the 0BCD residue model gives P = O^{d_1}[-1] locally, so E is finite locally free. Edge cases checked: empty base or fibre, X = S, P^1 and elliptic families, degree-2 etale cover excluded, disconnected base, non-flat g.
